notes: Customer profile: national telco with low-latency chat assistants for customer service and real-time call summarization.
Primary ask: Dedicated GPU capacity with hard throughput guarantees and a documented multi-region failover plan. Wants explicit headroom numbers and failover timing.
Target SLOs discussed: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 200ms for 512-token chat; steady-state throughput target = 350 req/s (avg payload ~120 tokens) with bursts to 700 req/s for 2-3 min windows.
Requested reserved pool sizing: propose 96 x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs across 3 regions (us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1) on an active-active with weighted routing plan.
Failover / headroom plan proposed by SE: 20-25% warm headroom per region + cross-region burst capacity (cold start warm-up ~60-90s for large models unless KV pre-warmed).
Customer prefers active-active routing for 60% west / 30% east / 10% eu, with automatic failover to nearest region on latency/error thresholds.
Cache strategy: prefix/KV cache replication recommended for p95 goals; cost trade-offs flagged — customer asked for quantified delta vs single-region cache.
Quantization/packing: Optimize team to propose INT8 quantized variants for non-critical inference (reranking/embeddings) to reduce reserved GPU footprint.
Negotiation items: SLA uptime for dedicated pools, explicit latency SLOs tied to credits/penalties, committed monthly baseline vs burst allowances, cross-region data transfer caps and pricing.
Quote request: detailed pricing for 96-GPU baseline + 25% headroom in standby across regions; alternative option: 64-GPU baseline + on-demand burst with guaranteed warm-up SLA.
Procurement notes: technical review positive; procurement wants a one-page appendix describing failover sequence (DNS routing, cache warm-up, KV snapshot restore timelines).
Direct quote from infra lead: "We need predictable tail latency — hectic with current cloud endpoints. Willing to commit if Redwood can guarantee p95 under our traffic profile."
Action items captured in drive: pricing deck, multi-region design doc, POC telemetry export (see linked_drive_docs).
Staleness risk: if SOC2 not delivered by 2026-03-22 they may pause contracting and re-evaluate other vendors.

Procurement requires SOC2 and an appendix defining failover timelines.
